subject: Planned staggered node reboots in westus2 — NIC driver update (May 7-8)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Westus2 NIC driver update — proposed staggered reboot plan

Team,

We’ve validated the upstream NIC driver (intel-ixgbe 6.4.2) that addresses a packet drop regression for instances with p4-like NICs. Kernel patch is small but requires node-level reboots to ensure firmware handshake completes. Based on current capacity and customer distribution in westus2, I propose a staggered/reduced-impact schedule across AZs:

- Phase A (May 7, 02:00-06:00 PDT): az-westus2-a — 20% of GPU nodes, maintenance window 4h
- Phase B (May 7, 08:00-12:00 PDT): az-westus2-b — 25% of GPU nodes, maintenance window 4h
- Phase C (May 8, 00:00-06:00 PDT): remaining nodes (rolling by rack, 10–15 minute per rack)

Rollback will be immediate: if packet loss or API error rate increases >1.5x baseline for 15m, we trigger automated rollback to current driver and rehydrate affected nodes from snapshot. Runbook and rollback checklist attached.

Action items:
- Monica: customer comms (short notice + staged windows + support path).
- Hannah: ops on-call for runbook execution and rollback automation.
- Laura: confirm SLA exceptions and sales-alert templates.

I’ll be on-call both nights. Thoughts?

—Rishi

Attachments: maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf, postpatch-rollback-checklist.md
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Seth Thompson <seth@acme.com>, acme-cloudops@acme.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Planned maintenance: NIC driver update in westus2 (May 7-8)

Seth / Acme Cloud Ops,

I’m reaching out with a planned maintenance update that will affect a subset of your workloads running in westus2. We are applying a NIC driver update to address a packet-handling regression observed at high p99 throughput. The update requires short, staggered node reboots. Our goal is to preserve capacity and avoid customer-visible interruptions, but some brief TCP connection drops and reconnections are possible during a node reboot.

Summary:
- What: NIC driver upgrade + node reboot (intel-ixgbe 6.4.2)
- When: May 7–8, 2026; windows are staggered by AZ to minimize impact (see schedule below)
- Expected impact: transient connection resets on affected nodes during reboot (autoscaling and retries should mitigate). No data loss expected.
- Mitigation: rolling approach, immediate rollback if error rates exceed thresholds, on-call operations monitoring

Schedule (local PDT):
- May 7, 02:00–06:00 — az-westus2-a (partial pool)
- May 7, 08:00–12:00 — az-westus2-b (partial pool)
- May 8, 00:00–06:00 — remaining nodes (rolling)

We are proactively disabling preemption on any reserved workloads during their AZ window and ensuring warm standby capacity. If you have critical maintenance windows, please reply with hosts or job ids to exclude before 05/06 23:59 PDT.

Support: we will post live updates to our status page and you can reach us via the normal support channel or directly reply here; Rishi and Hannah will be on-call and monitoring.

Apologies for the short notice; this patch reduces rare p99 packet drops seen over the last two weeks.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf
From: Seth Thompson <seth@acme.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, acme-cloudops@acme.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: NIC driver update in westus2 (May 7-8)

Thanks for the heads up, Monica.

A couple quick asks from our side:
1) Can you exclude the 3 reserved inference clusters we have (acme-inf-1, acme-inf-2, acme-inf-3)? Those run customer-facing models at peak times and can't be interrupted.
2) Can you confirm whether this is a kernel-level change or just the driver? Any rolling restart will break open sockets and we want to coordinate client-side retry/backoff windows.

If you can confirm exclusions before 05/06 23:59 PDT we’ll be fine. Otherwise we’ll reroute critical traffic.

—Seth
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Seth Thompson <seth@acme.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 17:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: NIC driver update in westus2 (May 7-8)

Seth — thanks for the notes. Short answers:
- Exclusions: we can pin acme-inf-1/2/3 out of the maintenance pool; Monica, I’ve added them to the exclusion list and updated the runbook.
- Scope: this is a driver + firmware handshake update; no kernel ABI changes. Reboots are needed to complete the firmware negotiation. We do NOT expect kernel-level module changes that require rebuilds.

Operational notes for customers:
- Expected disruption: intermittent TCP resets during the node reboot window for workloads scheduled on affected hosts (10–60s).
- Client guidance: exponential backoff with jitter; if you rely on long-lived sessions, consider short-lived reconnects in the client or sticky session pinning to excluded nodes.

Rollback criteria (we will publish thresholds during the run):
- api_error_rate (5m) > 1.5x baseline OR
- p50_latency increase > 30% sustained for 5m OR
- Increase in failed health checks per node > 3 within 10m

We’ll send a final confirmation once exclusions are complete and the runbook is staged.

—Hannah
